title: Guided Allocator: rightsizing recommendations and utilization baselining for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a Guided Allocator that produces actionable rightsizing recommendations for Dedicated GPU pools by combining historic utilization baselines, tail-latency budgets, and workload shape clustering. The feature should surface: pool-level recommended commit (vGPU/GPU counts), suggested autoscale floor/ceiling/burst settings, expected monthly cost delta, and confidence bands.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Produce recommendations for at least 90% of existing Dedicated pools used in the last 90 days.
- Recommendations include: (a) new target commit (nodes/GPUs), (b) autoscale policy proposal, (c) expected cost delta and 95th-percentile latency impact estimate.
- Console: Add a single-card recommendation with CTA to apply or export as a change request (CSV and CLI).
- CLI/SDK: Exportable plan and a dry-run simulator to project throughput and cost under proposed sizing.
- Safety: Never recommend >30% reduction in committed GPUs for pools with SLO breaches in past 30 days; flag pools with regression risk.
- Telemetry: Add sampling and rollup metrics for recommended vs applied delta and post-apply SLA regressions.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: historical utilization aggregation (per-node and per-GPU), workload clustering (latency-sensitive vs throughput-batched), simple cost model (region price * GPU-hours + marginal infra), UI card and CSV export, backend recommendation service and scheduler for retries.
- Out-of-scope for this ticket: automated enforced downsizing (must be manual-apply), complex market-based pricing, or integration with sales/contracting flows.

Technical approach:
1) Data aggregation pipeline: nightly rollups of per-request metrics (tokens/sec, request size, p95/p99 latency, queue depth) by pool and by model. Use existing telemetry sources (metrics-pipeline queries) and store summary in recommendations-store.
2) Workload classification: k-means clustering on time-windowed features to label workloads (interactive, streaming, batch). Use clusters to set latency risk multipliers.
3) Rightsizing heuristic: combine peak-buffered utilization (peak minus KV-cache reuse), tail-latency headroom, and frequency-of-peaks to compute a utilization-adjusted target commit. Score proposal with a confidence metric (low/medium/high).
4) Cost projection: hourly cost model with reservation amortization and burst costs; present delta as absolute $/month and percent.
5) UI/CLI: new recommendation endpoint, Console card with explanations and toggles (conservative/aggressive), export to CSV + CLI apply command.

Data and queries required:
- 90-day per-pool CPU/GPU utilization rolling 1m/5m/1h buckets.
- Per-request latency histograms by model and pool (p50/p95/p99).
- Autoscale event history and applied commit sizes.
- Billing unit prices per region and GPU SKU.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal-only for infra and SRE teams (2 weeks) — gather feedback on recommendations quality.
- Beta: opt-in for top 25 Dedicated customers (4 weeks) — measure conversion and SLA regressions.
- GA: Console-wide availability with guardrails (1 month).

Monitoring and KPIs:
- % pools with recommendations applied within 30 days.
- Post-apply SLA regression frequency (target <= 2% of applies).
- Avg cost savings per pool applied (target > 8% for non-burst workloads).
- False-positive reduction rate after model updates.

Risks and mitigations:
- Regression risk for latency-sensitive workloads: include conservative mode and require canary/gradual apply.
- Data sparsity for new pools: fallback to heuristic based on similar pools and mark low confidence.
- Pricing complexity: hide edge-case fees and surface known caveats in UI.

Open implementation decisions:
- Whether to persist recommendation history in existing infra or a new lightweight store (trade-off: query performance vs engineering overhead).
- How to surface confidence bands visually in Console (numeric vs traffic-simulated overlay).

Acceptance tests:
- Unit tests for rightsizing heuristic and cost projection.
- Integration tests with metrics pipeline and billing prices.
- End-to-end smoke test: run on a synthetic traffic generator and verify that recommended commit yields latency within tolerance in the simulator.

Deliverables:
- Backend recommendation service, REST API, and nightly job for rollups.
- Console card and CSV export + CLI apply/dry-run.
- Documentation in Confluence: recommendations playbook and evaluation checklist.
comments: 2025-11-12 - Initial architecture review with infra and telemetry teams. Decided to reuse nightly rollup infra to avoid high cardinality Spark jobs. (notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/REC-alloc)
2025-11-14 - Marco: prototype of utilization aggregator available (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alloc-recs/pull/92). Needs additional labels for KV-cache reuse metric.
2025-11-17 - Data team: confirmed availability of GPU-hour pricing per region via billing API; added to dependencies. (issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/issues/211)
2025-11-19 - SRE review: to avoid accidental regression we will gate 'apply' with a canary job that runs on 5% traffic and monitors p95 for 30 minutes before full apply.

2025-11-21 - Design feedback from Lena Chen: Console card should show three proposal tiers (conservative/standard/aggressive) and tooltip explaining confidence calculation. (Figma: https://figma.com/file/rdw-guided-alloc)

2025-11-24 - Marco: Added simulation dry-run CLI (alpha) and exported CSV format. Next: integrate simulator with Console for projected latency overlay (todo). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alloc-recs/pull/118
